messages:
Sam: quick flag 1: our internal worker called the generate endpoint and got 401, but it was sending x-redwood-org and x-redwood-project. intended?
Kelly: Authorization header is required. org/project headers are scoping only after successful auth. missing Authorization -> 401.
Aditya: TL;DR: must send "Authorization: Bearer <key>". flow: 1) auth header presence/validity -> 401 if absent/invalid, 2) permission to requested org/project -> 403 if not allowed, 3) continue.
Sam: ok that explains it. small follow-up: policy for rotated keys? old key used during rotation should fail or be accepted during grace?
Aditya: we accept old keys while they're in the rotation grace window. default grace = 600s (10m), configurable. after grace expires it becomes 401. keys in "rotating" state still authenticate.
Marta: what about passing api key as query param (?api_key=...) — legacy clients still do this.
Kelly: query param deprecated (2023-11). current runtime ignores it and emits a warning in logs. only Authorization header supported for API keys now.
ci-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/docs/auth#headers :link: (perm: eng)
Marta: error payload shape? integrations need stable codes.
Kelly: response body is JSON with fields: code, message, details. auth codes: "unauthenticated" -> 401 and "forbidden" -> 403. example:
```
{
  "code": "unauthenticated",
  "message": "missing Authorization header",
  "details": []
}
```
Aditya: also note we emit a rotation hint header when a rotating key is used: `x-redwood-rotate-info: grace=600,new-key-id=key_ABC`. clients can use that to detect a rotation in progress.
Sam: neat. any special behavior for global infra keys vs project-scoped keys?
Aditya: yes. keys have scope metadata: global/org/project. if key is global, x-redwood-project is optional (we still apply project quotas if provided). if key is project-scoped and request omits x-redwood-project -> return 403. if key is valid but not authorized for the provided project -> 403.
Kelly: header casing: we normalize, so X-Redwood-Org and x-redwood-org both accepted. still recommend lower-case in examples.
Sam: how should SDKs surface transient vs permanent auth failures?
Aditya: recommendation: exponential backoff + jitter on 401s. treat short spikes (<30s) as likely rotation. if 401s persist across multiple hosts for >30s, escalate as probable permanent invalidation. also watch for `x-redwood-rotate-info` to detect rotation activity and avoid immediate operator alerts.
Marta: can we get a canonical curl example for the README/SDK docs?
ci-bot: example curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer key_live_..." \
  -H "x-redwood-org: org_42" \
  -H "x-redwood-project: proj_99" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Kelly: I'll add a tiny API-contract note and a regression suite test asserting the 401 v 403 ordering (i.e., missing auth -> 401 even if scope headers present).
Sam: I'll patch the service SDK to always set Authorization and interpret x-redwood-rotate-info to surface a softer alert. will also remove query-param fallback.
Aditya: if Dedicated pilot needs a longer rotation window we can raise grace to 900s (15m) temporarily. ping me.
Marta: thanks all, closing this loop :thumbsup:
